review.slaps: Card-dealing demo: highest random card wins immediately, without a player decision or slap mechanic.
review.geom-storm: Renderer stress showcase; retain as a benchmark rather than a default arcade game.
review.halloween-words: Unfinished candy prototype: scoring empties the bag before the spider penalty can matter.
review.wat: Unfinished tower defense: broken wave/enemy lifecycle and no base-health loss loop.
review.sunside: Character, outfit and camera showcase with a short attached rally.
review.squarer: Collision/Frogger prototype lacks a finished progression, ending and replay.
review.hot-potato: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.iron-keep: Repair hold: all nine required visual/audio assets are still placeholders.
review.aquarium-forever 5: Earlier Bigger Tank implementation, superseded by Aquarium Forever: Beyond the Surface.
review.blank-template: Empty starter template; no game loop.
review.image-gallery: Image display demo; retain for asset testing.
review.ball-bounce: Basic bounce/score prototype; both dddd and ims archives contain this same game.
review.dance-fever: Movement/scoring prototype without a timed round or result.
review.two-player-fight: Shared-keyboard combat sketch; Block Brawlers is the developed alternative.
review.dump-truck: Vehicle movement sketch; Happy Haulers and Red Truck Ramble develop this idea.
review.robots-arena: Basic robot combat sketch; retain for comparison with Block Brawlers and the arena games.
review.soccer: Early soccer/combat sketch with shared controls; needs a complete match and restart.
review.neon-shooter: Early wave shooter; Polystorm and Doodle Invaders provide more developed alternatives.
review.neon-dodge: Small survival prototype; retain for review alongside the more developed arcade games.
review.city-scanner: Earlier living-city exploration; Little Consequences develops the simulation and Common Ground adds building decisions.
review.city-commons: Intermediate city diorama; Little Consequences is the fuller living-world exploration.
review.railway-reverie: Earlier model railway world; Little Consequences carries forward its trains, traffic and independent cameras.
review.counterforge-wilds: Broad procedural RPG overlaps Copperline. Keep the distinctive learning-opponent idea in Counterforge: Apex.
review.warpoint: Small conquest RTS overlaps the deeper Vector Siege and more approachable Pocket Front.
review.doodle-invaders: Earlier wave shooter; Polystorm supplies the campaign shmup and Nova Guard keeps cooperative defense.
review.grand-finale: Earlier fireworks chain-reaction game; Lumen Festival develops this role.
review.zap-tap: Single reflex minigame; Micro Mayhem provides a broader party challenge.
review.flick: Physics scoring sketch without a developed match arc; Tumble Tower and Dragon Drop offer clearer goals.
review.cabinet: CHIP-8 emulator showcase with Pong; keep as a technical demo rather than a standalone showcase game.
review.prism-3d: Earlier first-person arena; After Hours expands this role with maps and modes.
review.testions: Question-upload party prototype; stronger authored rounds and clearer entry in Fakeout and Imposter.
review.text-input: Shared typing demo. Draw remains the flexible creative canvas and Wordforge turns typing into a game.
review.bunny-harvest: Simple timed carrot collection without enough variety or feedback for the general showcase.
review.aquarium: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.bannerbound: The personal combat plus conquest idea is promising, but the tiny units, dense mode controls and sparse battle feedback need a larger presentation and onboarding redesign. Pocket Front and Vector Siege currently communicate their strategy more clearly.
review.blackjack: Complete rules, but the sparse generic card table does not distinguish itself as a showcase experience. Needs tactile dealing, chip handling and stronger round presentation before returning.
review.crazy-eights: Functional private-hand rules, but the same sparse table presentation and small cards add little distinct appeal to the showcase. Needs a focused card-table interaction and visual pass.
review.dots-and-boxes: A bare grid with standard rules offers little discovery or personality after the first few moves. Preserve the implementation as a compact board-game example.
review.go-fish: The generic card table and repeated rank requests have little visual or interactive reward. Needs readable illustrated sets and more satisfying collection feedback.
review.hearts: The rules are developed, but a newcomer faces a dense hand and rule-dependent decisions without a distinctive table experience. Preserve for a dedicated card-game polish pass.
review.spades: Bidding, nils and bags require substantial prior knowledge while the presentation is a small generic card table. Needs clearer trick feedback and onboarding before a general showcase.
review.tic-tac-toe: The standard three-by-three game is useful as a simple framework example, but has too little discovery or replay depth to earn a showcase slot.
review.disco-owl: A rhythm-combat premise needs an audible musical beat and coherent enemy presentation. Current combat uses a visual beat with placeholder enemy/background art; UI trimming cannot finish that core experience.
review.keep-up: The timed balloon loop works, but the nearly empty playfield and repeated identical taps lack enough variety or tactile character. Needs more distinct balloon behavior and stronger visual feedback.
review.raft: The shared steering joke is understandable, but the long run repeats a sparse river and duck collection without enough encounters. Needs authored river events and a stronger pace curve.
review.star-sweeper: Independent cameras are technically useful, but long travel across a sparse field of identical collectibles creates too much downtime. Tug Club gives shared space a clearer physical objective.
review.sponge: The sink-themed Pong loop is playable, but the flat stretched court and limited surprise do not meet the current presentation bar. Keep for a more substantial art and paddle-feel revision.
review.the-argument: The asymmetric briefings are distinctive, but the 30-minute text-led session demands too much setup before a new visitor sees a payoff. Needs shorter authored scenarios and a tested social round flow.
review.weed-smoke-willie: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.little-slugger: Gentle assisted batting is appropriate for young children, but the authored outcomes and repeated target selection offer limited engagement for the general showcase audience. Preserve for a dedicated early-childhood collection.
review.rainbow-pop: The color-matching balloon toy is attractive but intentionally shallow for general curious players. Keep as an early-childhood activity; the main catalog has richer creative toys.
review.starry-sparkles: The fireworks painting toy is gentle but overlaps the more reactive Lumen Festival and the shared Draw canvas. Preserve for an early-childhood collection.
review.after-hours: Internal test / review: Hold for a dedicated shooter/performance pass. Arena maps and modes are substantial, but the measured eight-player scene traffic is too expensive for ordinary home uplinks; this also needs weapon feel, navigation and real-group validation beyond launch smoke tests.
review.backgammon: Internal test / review: The rules and bot are developed, but the small generic table needs a dedicated teaching and tactile presentation pass. Billiards is the stronger immediate physical table-game choice for this smaller launch.
review.backstage: Internal test / review: Eight framework experiments are useful learning material, but their purpose is to demonstrate Homegames features. Preserve as a developer test/example rather than ask a player looking for a game to choose it.
review.battleship: Internal test / review: Private grids and ship placement work as a rules implementation, but the sparse table and repeated coordinate hunting need more personality and payoff to earn one of the limited launch slots.
review.billiards: Keep for launch polish: Aiming, strength and cushion shots offer a tactile skill game; the bot makes it playable immediately without arranging a group.
review.block-brawlers: Internal test / review: The first-to-three fight is real, but the small procedural fighters and several attack/guard controls need a dedicated readability and combat-feel pass. More attack systems alone would not make this a strong general entry point.
review.buddy-box: Internal test / review: The central loop is damaging a ragdoll to buy more tools. The sparse scene and tool-shop discovery need a stronger expressive payoff and clear activity arc before this earns a public slot alongside Tumble Tower.
review.checkers: Internal test / review: Legal moves, dragging and bots are useful, but the same small standard table adds breadth more than a distinctive Homegames experience. Keep the implementation for a future focused board-game collection.
review.chess: Internal test / review: A complete rules implementation is valuable, but the current generic table lacks a distinctive teaching, social or presentation reason to choose it here. A polished chess offering deserves its own focused effort rather than incidental inclusion.
review.chronoclast: Internal test / review: Replaying six seconds of combat as an ally is promising, but the sparse geometric combat and multiple simultaneous movement/fire/dash/echo actions make its best idea hard to appreciate quickly. Needs a focused encounter and feedback redesign.
review.clicktionary: Keep for launch polish: The players supply fresh drawings and guesses every round. It has a clear social payoff and a recap worth sharing.
review.clump: Internal test / review: Growing by collecting increasingly large objects has a satisfying premise, but the distant, tiny shapes make scale changes and what can be collected hard to read. Needs a substantial camera, object and collision-feedback pass.
review.common-ground: Internal test / review: Roads, zones and metrics simulate a town, but the dense tools and small buildings ask for systems learning before a strong personal goal emerges. Hold for a focused city-building experience rather than another broad simulation.
review.connect-four: Internal test / review: The familiar rules and bot make this usable, but the standard sparse table has little distinct personality. Retain as a compact example; the smaller catalog can provide immediate competition through Swish and Neon Grid.
review.copperline: Internal test / review: The RPG includes combat, missions, equipment and property, but that breadth brings a large onboarding and campaign-writing burden. Hold until the opening mission and moment-to-moment combat justify maintaining the entire adventure.
review.counterforge-apex: Internal test / review: The learning-opponent experiment is interesting, but tiny combat presentation and an intentionally unbeatable final form need a clearer player-facing payoff and fairness story. Preserve as an experiment pending a focused duel redesign.
review.deadword: Internal test / review: Typing words to stop waves provides a loop, but small text under time pressure and keyboard-led input narrow its appeal. It needs stronger enemy character, readable targeting and a convincing mobile interaction before inclusion.
review.defuse: Keep for launch polish: Different information on each screen gives people a concrete reason to talk and cooperate. This earns a separate slot from ordinary quizzes.
review.desert-bloom: Internal test / review: Watering and shading one cactus reaches a bloom, then resets the same small activity. It needs more expressive choices or meaningful variety to sustain return visits; Aquarium and Little Rambler cover longer care play.
review.dragon-drop: Keep for launch polish: Drag, tumble and matching provide an immediate, repeatable physical puzzle. The current version has character art, cancellation handling and bounded physics.
review.draw: Keep for launch polish: An open shared canvas serves drawing, hanging out and making things together. It is useful beyond a scored round and belongs alongside the games.
review.draw-your-own-boss: Keep for launch polish: Making a monster and then fighting it connects creation to play in one short loop; the player's own drawing gives the encounter a personal payoff.
review.engine-room: Internal test / review: Shouting mismatched repair orders can work socially, but its grid of abstract controls overlaps Defuse's clearer shared emergency. Concentrate real-group onboarding and communication testing on Defuse first.
review.facet: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.fakeout: Internal test / review: Bluff trivia has social potential, but fixed fact quality and the writing/voting/reveal presentation need editorial work. Imposter and Clicktionary provide more immediate social play without this extra authored trivia burden.
review.fleetfall: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.gold-and-grit: Keep for launch polish: Fixed, previewed tower-defense waves, branching upgrades and editable maps give clear choices and durable replay value. It provides a longer strategy experience.
review.hangman: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.happy-haulers: Keep for launch polish: Choosing a project and colors produces a visible finished construction. This is a purposeful, readable activity for young children rather than another general arcade game.
review.house-band: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.imposter: Keep for launch polish: A secret word, conversation and a vote are easy to explain; players generate the variety and phones suit the private information.
review.kaboom-valley: Keep for launch polish: Aiming against wind and changing terrain gives each shot an understandable consequence. Local rivals can create replay value without a long campaign.
review.lemonade-tycoon: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.little-consequences: Internal test / review: The living diorama has many reactive systems, but much of the activity is moving a camera and triggering events. It needs a clearer personal project or expressive interaction to turn observation into sustained play.
review.little-rambler: Keep for launch polish: Care, two outings and useful home projects form a coherent return loop with a companion. It offers a different pace from the featured arcade games.
review.little-scoop-shop: Internal test / review: A gentle, coherent child activity, but serving a decorated treat substantially overlaps Tiny Bean Café. Keep one stronger serving loop and preserve this as an alternative for a later children's collection.
review.little-zoo-walk: Internal test / review: Feeding, catch and stamps are approachable for children, but six similar visits add another short tap-through activity. Focus the initial child collection on the more visibly constructive Happy Haulers and recipe-based Tiny Bean Café.
review.lumen-festival: Internal test / review: The fireworks are attractive, but launching bursts and chaining lanterns presently offers less personal authorship than House Band or Draw and less goal-driven play than the kept arcade games. Needs a clearer expressive or skill-based return loop.
review.mancala: Internal test / review: Captures, extra turns and a bot establish the classic game, but the small standard board needs a tactile sowing and teaching pass. Preserve the rules implementation without expanding the launch's generic board-game shelf.
review.masterpiece: Keep for launch polish: Dragging tiles to restore a visible painting is immediately understandable, and its finite three-work collection gives a clear completion goal.
review.micro-mayhem: Internal test / review: Five short reflex/memory tests offer variety, but their flat tile-and-text presentation makes them feel like exercises more than a memorable party. Needs a cohesive personality and group-tested pacing before returning.
review.midnight-movers: Keep for launch polish: Carrying oversized loot through guards and obstacles creates shared physical problems. Three authored heists and medals supply a manageable polish target.
review.moonbounce: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.mouth-house: Keep for launch polish: Combining food clues to feed a changing creature gives a small deduction puzzle with a visible reward. It works solo and gains conversation with friends.
review.neon-grid: Keep for launch polish: Steering into open space and trapping opponents has a readable short-round skill loop. Bots let someone find the fun before inviting friends.
review.nova-guard: Internal test / review: Moving shields around a shared core is simple to explain, but the abstract wave-defense presentation provides less memorable shared action than Tug Club's visible hauling and building. Hold for enemy variety and impact/readability work.
review.one-unreasonable-hole: Keep for launch polish: Building a course and challenging a friend makes players' ideas the replay content. It directly supports keeping and sharing something personal.
review.orbit-breaker: Internal test / review: Catching and returning fire is a strong specialist premise, but twin-stick movement, timed counterattacks and a dark sparse field need substantial combat teaching and feel work. Keep as a future focused action title, not extra launch volume.
review.pitch-pot: Internal test / review: Recording sales pitches asks for writing, microphone permission and performance before the group gets a payoff. Its social setup and recordings need a separate real-group polish pass; prioritize lower-friction party games first.
review.pocket-front: Keep for launch polish: A six-wave defense run with troop placement and upgrade choices is a contained, replayable introduction to strategy, distinct from Gold & Grit's fixed campaign.
review.polystorm: Internal test / review: The staged shmup and bosses provide content, but sparse geometric enemies, small targets and a keyboard-led high-speed loop need a larger presentation and accessibility pass. Stage count alone does not earn a slot.
review.pulsefront: Internal test / review: Sending forces between nodes overlaps featured Fleetfall's strategy layer. Keep Fleetfall's direct piloting as the distinctive version and avoid maintaining several visually similar conquest games at launch.
review.red-truck-ramble: Internal test / review: Driving, flipping and honking are pleasant but the cruise loop has less player-directed construction than Happy Haulers. Keep the latter as the clearer vehicle activity in the small child selection.
review.relic-rush: Internal test / review: Lane dodging, jumping and ducking form a familiar runner, but the plain corridor and repeated obstacles need a stronger visual identity and encounter progression. Watching one person run also adds little to the multiplayer promise.
review.sandy-castle: Internal test / review: Making and washing a sandcastle is a valid gentle toy, but it overlaps the retained construction and pretend-play activities. Preserve it for a dedicated child collection rather than fill the launch with similar short loops.
review.seance: Internal test / review: Shared planchette movement is an amusing experiment, but its enjoyment relies heavily on players inventing a performance around a letter board. Needs authored surprises and clearer agency before it is a dependable standalone activity.
review.sheep-drive: Internal test / review: Herding through three timed fields can be fun, but the bare field and small flock need much stronger character and steering feedback. Concentrate cooperative physics polish on Midnight Movers and Tug Club first.
review.showboat: Internal test / review: Live-camera improvisation can be social, but it imposes permission, performance and group-coordination friction before the first payoff. Hold for a dedicated real-person camera-party trial and clearer onboarding.
review.snap-judgment: Internal test / review: A household photo scavenger hunt is distinct, but photographing, uploading and waiting for a judge makes a slow first round. Needs real-phone/group pacing and prompt editing before inclusion in an immediate-play launch.
review.starfall-salvage: Internal test / review: The adventure has crew, equipment, travel and story, but its dense menus and broad campaign need sustained writing and pacing work. Defer until one complete opening episode establishes an engaging moment-to-moment experience.
review.starweld: Internal test / review: Ship upgrades and four bosses are developed, but another dark geometric space-combat campaign dilutes the collection. Needs more readable attachment effects and a stronger first battle to compete for a future action slot.
review.sundown: Internal test / review: Distance racing has immediate movement, but repeating the road before sunset offers limited distinct decisions and payoff. Needs traffic/route character and a stronger run progression rather than just a distance score.
review.sunwake: Internal test / review: Crew roles and a cooperative skyship expedition are promising, but role assignment, navigation and campaign systems demand a larger group-polish effort. Tug Club provides the clearer shared-vehicle objective for this launch.
review.swarmwell: Internal test / review: Growing nests and sending swarms is another node-conquest game. Its food/frenzy systems add explanation without enough separation from featured Fleetfall; hold for a more distinctive colony interaction.
review.swish: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.tabletop-railway: Keep for launch polish: Trains crossing physically adjacent screens make multiplayer tangible. Twelve deliveries provide a finite shared objective, with solo practice available.
review.tiny-bean-cafe: Keep for launch polish: Large pictured tools, animal requests and seven recipes make a coherent pretend-play activity. It earns one of two focused young-child slots.
review.tug-club: Keep for launch polish: Attaching to cargo and hauling it home is a simple cooperative physical interaction. The home visibly improves, giving a round a shared payoff.
review.tumble-tower: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.vector-siege: Internal test / review: Fleet command plus direct combat overlaps featured Fleetfall while adding a dense persistent-war layer. Keep the clearer featured hybrid and defer this larger strategy simulation.
review.vegas-trail: Keep for launch polish: Protected maintainer choice from homegamesio/site.config.json. Keep and polish; inclusion is not a claim that QA is finished.
review.walkie-talkie: Internal test / review: Push-to-talk and microphone access demonstrate communication, but there is no game objective or expressive creation loop. Preserve as a media test rather than a release game.
review.wordforge: Internal test / review: Turning words into platforms is a good experiment, but simultaneous typing, movement and rising-flood pressure split attention and fit phones awkwardly. Needs a simpler first interaction that makes word choices matter visibly.
review.world-eater: Internal test / review: The cooperative cosmic campaign includes progression, guardians and endings, but the tiny abstract action and broad systems require a dedicated legibility and pacing pass. Keep the clearer short cooperative loops while this develops.
review.worldseed: Internal test / review: Secret choices and a shared world reveal are an interesting social system, but four abstract powers and metric changes need clearer causal feedback and player stories. Hold until repeated rounds demonstrate more than a simulation reveal.

showcase.bar: A clear first action, a distinctive or satisfying core interaction, worthwhile feedback and a reason to play another round. Familiar classics can stay when they offer a polished, approachable table.
showcase.preserved: All game source and assets remain available with TESTS_ENABLED=true.

polishedThisPass.chess: Drag pieces with a lifted preview, legal destinations and hand cursors. Illegal drops return the piece; tap moves still work.
polishedThisPass.checkers: Drag checkers and kings; preserve legal moves, jump rules and tap controls. Destination dots now accept clicks.
polishedThisPass.billiards: Aim using a relative drag from anywhere on the table. Taps do not accidentally shoot; hand cursors show when aiming is available.
polishedThisPass.dragon-drop: Drag a color card into the pit and release once. Preview the held color, retain tap selection, and cancel outside the pit.
polishedThisPass.masterpiece: Large portrait painting, constrained tile dragging, three original artworks, a gentler opening shuffle and deliberate progression after completion.
polishedThisPass.tumble-tower: Drag a ball or block directly from the tool palette into play; retain immediate tap-to-throw controls.
polishedThisPass.draw: New players join the existing drawing view and can pan independently. Pen and eraser cursors show the current tool.

showcase.sharedInputFix: Preserve the original press point and flush the final movement before release, including gestures completed between animation frames.

catalogBrowser.scope: Offline Chrome launch, first frame and representative game scene; no external asset requests or browser errors.

currentNodeTests.scope: Existing .test.cjs game suites except the four retired Tremulous files; pointer lock, relative motion and touch focus contracts included.

verification.cursorBrowser: Passed local host, RTC guest, WebSocket inline and worker transports, player isolation and disconnect reset.
verification.swishBrowser: Passed mouse/touch drags, short guide, theme locking, persisted records and real RTC ball collisions/individual scoring.
verification.clientBuild: Built homegames-client and synchronized the bundle to core and homegamesio. Existing webpack bundle-size warnings remain.
verification.thumbnails: All 73 showcase thumbnails regenerated from real browser scenes; manifest and catalog audit pass.
verification.previousUiReviewFailures: Resolved the three Little Scoop Shop/Little Zoo Walk frame-test fixture errors: use the current snapshot serializer and keep the session runtime open while controlling its tick interval.
broaderRunLimitations: Four existing Tremulous test files reference absent src/games/tremulous sources. They remain unchanged and are excluded from the current-game .test.cjs run.

The exact prerecorded Moonbounce adventure route for The Patient Pendulum passes under Node 18 but differs under Node 24. The cross-version route fixture remains unresolved; the game source was not changed in this pass.
verification.limits: Browser smoke coverage and selected interaction checks are not exhaustive playthroughs or a substitute for outside-player feedback.
